Make rollback real. W5 (#2227) shipped the canary-gated fleet train, kill switch, pin honesty, operator panel, bp cloud truth, and curator digest — and its charter D7 named the one honest gap: 'rollback v1 = surfaced pinning; the blue/green Caddy port-flip rollback API is a named W6 candidate, not a fake button this wave.' W6 ships that verb end-to-end IF the honest design holds: instance-side flip-to-previous-slot (reusing the sanctioned instance-deploy machinery), CP relay route with pin integration (rolling back PINS at the rolled-back version — an unpinned rollback re-updates on the next cron tick, which is a lie), console button + bp cloud twin (D36), health-gated fail-closed, and deny-path tests (no previous slot → honest error; pinned instance → coherent with pin semantics). If port-flip can't be proven safe without the human-gated staging box, scope honestly to what the offline harness + fake transports CAN prove and park the live smoke with a recipe.

One honest path, no new capabilities: the rollback verb lives ON THE INSTANCE as a mode of the sanctioned deploy machinery (instance-deploy.sh --rollback or a sibling sharing its functions), and rides the SAME CP→instance relay seam the Update button already uses. Charter D3 holds absolutely: no CP→SSH bridge, no repo checkout on the CP.

The finished experience: an operator staring at a bad release clicks Rollback in the console (or runs bp cloud rollback <instance>), the instance boots its previous slot, health-gates it, flips Caddy only on green, and the fleet view now shows the rolled-back version WITH a pin at that version — the cron tick cannot silently undo the operator's decision. Every refusal is typed and honest: no previous slot build → error that says so; previous slot boots dead → fail closed, Caddy untouched, error says so; instance pinned → response coherent with pin semantics.

Known hard problems the survey must resolve before Decide: (a) SLOT-VERSION AMNESIA — instance-deploy.sh records only the NEW sha in its STATE file; nothing records what version the now-idle slot holds, so rollback likely needs a per-slot version stamp written at deploy time (and must refuse when the stamp is missing/stale). (b) SHARED STATIC HAZARD — priv/static is shared source symlinked into both slots and the wasm blob is rebuilt per deploy; flipping back may serve OLD beam with NEW static assets unless rollback also moves sources/rebuilds. (c) SCHEMA STAYS FORWARD — ecto.migrate already ran for NEW; rollback is app-level only and must say so (expand/contract is the safety argument, verify it is law). (d) OPERATOR GATE — W5 left the kill-switch routes worker-token-gated and operator-unreachable; the rollback relay route must use a gate the console session and bp cloud can actually pass, without inventing a third principal model.

Fallback posture if exploration breaks the design: ship the instance-side machinery + offline-harness proof (the 49-check harness gains rollback cases) + CP route + surfaces wired but guarded, and park the live smoke as a written recipe against a disposable box (never a casual live-flip on guerrilla, which is production).

content.value: (1) SLOT-VERSION AMNESIA is real: .instance-deploy-last holds one global sha (instance-deploy.sh:59,290); .slots/*.env carry only PORT_OVERRIDE+MIX_BUILD_ROOT (:189-190); nothing records what the idle slot's build corresponds to, and the NEXT deploy rm -rf's exactly that build (:199). Rollback needs a per-slot version stamp written at deploy time and must refuse when it is missing. (2) WORSE THAN THE CHARTER ASSUMED — both slots run `mix phx.server` against ONE SHARED git checkout (barkpark-slot@.service:15-16 -> api/start.sh:36-38); MIX_BUILD_ROOT isolates only the _build cache, and the checkout is never reset back on a successful deploy. Restarting the idle slot after HEAD moved forward likely triggers Mix to recompile NEW source into the OLD slot's build root — the 'instant manual rollback' comment (:264-265) is asserted, never tested. This is the single biggest design threat and is INFERRED, not yet proven; the verify fleet proves or refutes it. (3) Shared-static hazard confirmed in the script's own words (:216-217): priv/static + the per-deploy-rebuilt wasm blob are shared into both slots — a flip serves old beam with newest assets. (4) Schema stays forward: one ecto.migrate on the NEW build (:204-205); expand/contract is a 3-place comment convention (deploy/README.md:29-30, instance-deploy.sh:16-17, cp-deploy.sh:15), unenforced, scoped to the swap window; the health gate is a shallow /api/schemas 200 (:234) — rollback copy must say app-level-only and what the gate does NOT prove. (5) The post-flip public curl (:260) is LOG-ONLY — copying it as rollback's gate would be a fake gate; the real gate is the pre-flip localhost loop (:232-243).

children.value: Relay + pin + truth loop, fully mapped.

content.value: Console button -> CP POST /v1/barkparks/:id/self-update (require_primary_team_admin, team-scoped 404, router.ex:1787) -> Registry.trigger_self_update (pin gate, Vault-decrypted per-instance admin token, synchronous :httpc 15s) -> instance POST /v1/admin/self-update (require_admin) -> Runner async OS Port -> scripts/self-update.sh -> exec deploy/instance-deploy.sh on .slots boxes. Rollback rides this exact chain as a sibling verb and MUST keep the async-Port shape (the CP relay times out at 15s). pinned_release is an unvalidated <=255-char string with exactly two readers: trigger refusal (registry.ex:2678) and rollout-worker candidate exclusion (is_nil, registry.ex:2791) — so a PINNED rollback is already immune to re-advancement with zero new logic, and an UNPINNED rollback is actively undone within one 5-min tick. The pin value must come from what the instance REPORTS it rolled back to, never operator free-text, and the existing pin gate must not block rollback (rollback re-pins by design). Version truth: BuildInfo is compile-time — the old slot reports the old release correctly once booted; the CP sees it at the hourly :17 cron unless the rollback route mirrors the trigger's schedule_in:60 UpdateStatusWorker enqueue + push_event('fleet'). A SECOND lying surface exists: barkpark-agent's git_commit = shared checkout HEAD (60s beat, report.go) — it lies after a bare flip unless the rollback resets checkout HEAD or the probe becomes slot-aware.

Make rollback real. W5 (#2227) shipped the canary-gated fleet train, kill switch, pin honesty, operator panel, bp cloud truth, and curator digest — and its charter D7 named the one honest gap: 'rollback v1 = surfaced pinning; the blue/green Caddy port-flip rollback API is a named W6 candidate, not a fake button this wave.' W6 ships that verb end-to-end IF the honest design holds: instance-side flip-to-previous-slot (reusing the sanctioned instance-deploy machinery), CP relay route with pin integration (rolling back PINS at the rolled-back version — an unpinned rollback re-updates on the next cron tick, which is a lie), console button + bp cloud twin (D36), health-gated fail-closed, and deny-path tests (no previous slot → honest error; pinned instance → coherent with pin semantics). If port-flip can't be proven safe without the human-gated staging box, scope honestly to what the offline harness + fake transports CAN prove and park the live smoke with a recipe.

One honest path, no new capabilities: the rollback verb lives ON THE INSTANCE as a mode of the sanctioned deploy machinery (instance-deploy.sh --rollback or a sibling sharing its functions), and rides the SAME CP→instance relay seam the Update button already uses. Charter D3 holds absolutely: no CP→SSH bridge, no repo checkout on the CP.

The finished experience: an operator staring at a bad release clicks Rollback in the console (or runs bp cloud rollback <instance>), the instance boots its previous slot, health-gates it, flips Caddy only on green, and the fleet view now shows the rolled-back version WITH a pin at that version — the cron tick cannot silently undo the operator's decision. Every refusal is typed and honest: no previous slot build → error that says so; previous slot boots dead → fail closed, Caddy untouched, error says so; instance pinned → response coherent with pin semantics.

Known hard problems the survey must resolve before Decide: (a) SLOT-VERSION AMNESIA — instance-deploy.sh records only the NEW sha in its STATE file; nothing records what version the now-idle slot holds, so rollback likely needs a per-slot version stamp written at deploy time (and must refuse when the stamp is missing/stale). (b) SHARED STATIC HAZARD — priv/static is shared source symlinked into both slots and the wasm blob is rebuilt per deploy; flipping back may serve OLD beam with NEW static assets unless rollback also moves sources/rebuilds. (c) SCHEMA STAYS FORWARD — ecto.migrate already ran for NEW; rollback is app-level only and must say so (expand/contract is the safety argument, verify it is law). (d) OPERATOR GATE — W5 left the kill-switch routes worker-token-gated and operator-unreachable; the rollback relay route must use a gate the console session and bp cloud can actually pass, without inventing a third principal model.

Barkpark · self-update-epic · wave 6 · living wave paper

Wave 6 — rollback becomes real

Epic task self-update-epic · Charter .claude/workflows/bp-self-update-w5-charter.md (self-update slot since W5) · Opened at Strategize 2026-07-11

STATUS: WAVE COMPLETE (Review, 2026-07-11). All 5 slices built green, reviewed, and handed to the lead for merge — the debrief closes this Paper below. (Correction note: this line read "VERIFYING" until Review; Decide appended its section without flipping it. The verify fleet and Decide sections below stand as written — no decision was reversed and no proof was superseded during Build.)

The wish

Make rollback real. W5 (#2227) shipped the canary-gated fleet train, kill switch, pin honesty, operator panel, bp cloud truth, and curator digest — and its charter D7 named the one honest gap: 'rollback v1 = surfaced pinning; the blue/green Caddy port-flip rollback API is a named W6 candidate, not a fake button this wave.' W6 ships that verb end-to-end IF the honest design holds: instance-side flip-to-previous-slot (reusing the sanctioned instance-deploy machinery), CP relay route with pin integration (rolling back PINS at the rolled-back version — an unpinned rollback re-updates on the next cron tick, which is a lie), console button + bp cloud twin (D36), health-gated fail-closed, and deny-path tests (no previous slot → honest error; pinned instance → coherent with pin semantics). If port-flip can't be proven safe without the human-gated staging box, scope honestly to what the offline harness + fake transports CAN prove and park the live smoke with a recipe.

Strategist direction (tentative — Decide finalizes)

One honest path, no new capabilities: the rollback verb lives ON THE INSTANCE as a mode of the sanctioned deploy machinery (instance-deploy.sh --rollback or a sibling sharing its functions), and rides the SAME CP→instance relay seam the Update button already uses. Charter D3 holds absolutely: no CP→SSH bridge, no repo checkout on the CP.

The finished experience: an operator staring at a bad release clicks Rollback in the console (or runs bp cloud rollback <instance>), the instance boots its previous slot, health-gates it, flips Caddy only on green, and the fleet view now shows the rolled-back version WITH a pin at that version — the cron tick cannot silently undo the operator's decision. Every refusal is typed and honest: no previous slot build → error that says so; previous slot boots dead → fail closed, Caddy untouched, error says so; instance pinned → response coherent with pin semantics.

Known hard problems the survey must resolve before Decide: (a) SLOT-VERSION AMNESIA — instance-deploy.sh records only the NEW sha in its STATE file; nothing records what version the now-idle slot holds, so rollback likely needs a per-slot version stamp written at deploy time (and must refuse when the stamp is missing/stale). (b) SHARED STATIC HAZARD — priv/static is shared source symlinked into both slots and the wasm blob is rebuilt per deploy; flipping back may serve OLD beam with NEW static assets unless rollback also moves sources/rebuilds. (c) SCHEMA STAYS FORWARD — ecto.migrate already ran for NEW; rollback is app-level only and must say so (expand/contract is the safety argument, verify it is law). (d) OPERATOR GATE — W5 left the kill-switch routes worker-token-gated and operator-unreachable; the rollback relay route must use a gate the console session and bp cloud can actually pass, without inventing a third principal model.

Fallback posture if exploration breaks the design: ship the instance-side machinery + offline-harness proof (the 49-check harness gains rollback cases) + CP route + surfaces wired but guarded, and park the live smoke as a written recipe against a disposable box (never a casual live-flip on guerrilla, which is production).

Terrain already skimmed at Strategize

deploy/instance-deploy.sh: per-slot build roots _build_blue/_build_green, Caddy upstream port = slot truth, health gate = curl /api/schemas 200 loop with --resolve, Caddyfile.pre-deploy backup + restore on failure, old slot RETIRED (disable --now) after 5s drain, comment names the manual rollback: 'flip the Caddyfile port back, reload caddy, start the old slot again'. instance-deploy_test.sh exists (the offline harness). scripts/{self-update,apply-update,local-update}.sh are the update-relay scripts. W5 charter (bp-self-update-w5-charter.md) carries D1-D10 + wave log with the operator-gate residue. Charter slot convention note: this file is the self-update epic's memory; the old cloud charter slot may hold a different epic — explorers reconcile.

Survey plan — 14 scouts, question + why

SLOT-MACHINERY-TRUTH — Map instance-deploy.sh end-to-end: exactly what state survives a deploy for the now-idle OLD slot (build root, disabled unit, Caddyfile backup, STATE file), and whether the old slot's git SHA is recorded ANYWHERE a rollback could read. WHY: Rollback must know what it is rolling back TO; if slot-version is amnesiac we must add a per-slot stamp at deploy time — that changes the slice plan.

SLOT-UNIT-RUNTIME — Read deploy/systemd/barkpark-slot@.service: compiled artifacts vs live sources, and what actually happens if the old slot unit starts while the checkout sits at the NEW sha; map the shared priv/static symlink + wasm blob implications of a flip-back. WHY: Decides whether rollback = pure port-flip or must also move sources/rebuild static — the difference between a 5-second flip and a rebuild-shaped verb.

MIGRATIONS-HAZARD — Determine what ecto.migrate having run for NEW means for a flipped-back OLD app; find where expand/contract discipline is documented as law (deploy/README, PROD_OPS, script comments). WHY: The rollback verb's honesty copy and health gate depend on whether old-code-on-new-schema is a supported invariant or a prayer.

UPDATE-RELAY-SEAM — Trace the CP Update button end-to-end today: console action → CP relay route → instance endpoint (controller + auth token in api/) → which script runs. Name every route, token, and timeout. WHY: The rollback verb should ride this exact seam (D3: no CP→SSH); we need the precise splice points.

SCRIPTS-TRIPLE — Disentangle scripts/self-update.sh vs apply-update.sh vs local-update.sh: who invokes whom, which path is sanctioned on blue/green slot boxes, and where the W5 pin-honest 409 landed. WHY: Rollback must reuse the sanctioned instance-side executor, and pin checks must not block a rollback that intentionally pins.

CP-PIN-MACHINERY — Map the CP registry: barkparks columns (pinned_release, channel, autoupdate_*), PATCH /v1/barkparks/:id/autoupdate semantics, AutoupdateRolloutWorker tick logic, and whether pinned_release accepts an arbitrary version string. WHY: Rollback must atomically pin at the rolled-back version; we need the exact write path and any validation that would reject it.

VERSION-TRUTH-LOOP — How does the CP learn an instance's running version (agent beat, update check, poll)? After a port-flip, by what path and how fast does the console show the rolled-back version — and does any reconciler fight it? WHY: If the fleet view lies for an hour after rollback, the feature reads as broken; and a reconciler that 'fixes' the version would re-update — the exact lie the pin prevents.

OPERATOR-GATE — How does the console SPA authenticate its pin/pause writes today (W5-S3), what gate do the D5 kill-switch routes use, and did anything post-#2227 add a platform-admin principal (PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS wiring status in runtime.exs / CP env)? WHY: The rollback route must be callable by the console session AND bp cloud; W5's residue warns two surfaces already invented two answers — we must not invent a third.

OFFLINE-HARNESS — Dissect deploy/instance-deploy_test.sh: how the 49 checks fake systemctl/caddy/curl/git, the assertion vocabulary, and the cheapest way to add rollback cases (happy flip, no-previous-slot refusal, unhealthy-old-slot fail-closed with Caddyfile restored). WHY: The wish makes the harness the proof spine — the rollback slices are only mergeable if these cases are natural to write.

CONSOLE-PANEL-SEAM — Map the cloud console update panel in cloud/priv/static/app.js: where per-instance actions render, the confirm/error patterns, noBounce lesson from W5-S3, and the __app.test.mjs harness idioms. WHY: The Rollback button lands here; the W5 review caught a logout-on-401 bug in this exact seam — we pre-load that knowledge.

CLI-TWIN-SEAM — Map internal/cli bp cloud verbs from W5-S4 (files, decode patterns, table output, exit codes) and where bp cloud rollback <instance> would land per the D36 console/CLI twin law. WHY: The CLI twin is a named deliverable; knowing the pattern makes it a small slice instead of an exploration.

PRIOR-ART-LEDGER — On guerrilla: read paper self-update-from-nag-to-product (rev 2) rollback mentions, bp-cloud-console-charter OC10 (repo file), and search tasks/papers for rollback / port-flip / blue-green prior art; confirm which charter file is the live self-update slot per the header-note convention. WHY: D7 pointed at OC10 — if a design sketch already exists we amend it rather than fork; and the charter-slot reconciliation is an explicit wish item.

HEALTHGATE-FLIP-MECHANICS — Extract the exact Caddyfile port-rewrite + reload + verify mechanics from instance-deploy.sh (sed/replace, .pre-deploy lifecycle, --resolve health curl) and what a STANDALONE rollback flip must replicate to fail closed without a deploy in flight. WHY: Rollback reuses this machinery but outside a deploy run — every assumption the deploy path makes (backup exists, both env files present) must be re-established or refused honestly.

STAGING-AND-SMOKE-RISK — Is a staging-channel box registered in the CP yet? Is golive-test.barkpark.cloud alive and disposable? What would a live rollback smoke need, and what makes guerrilla itself too risky (it is the production content API)? WHY: Decides the wish's fork: full live-proven verb vs offline-proven verb + parked smoke recipe. Also: the staging box would be the RIGHT place to ever smoke this.

DENY-PATH-SEMANTICS — Enumerate every refusal the rollback verb needs across layers: instance (no previous slot, stamp missing, unhealthy boot), CP (instance offline, already rolling out, halted fleet, pinned), CLI/console surfacing; check how W5 typed its errors (error.pinned_release precedent). WHY: Deny paths are half the wish; a shared typed-error vocabulary designed early keeps three surfaces coherent instead of three dialects.

Hard constraints (verbatim for every later phase)

guerrilla deploys ONLY via instance-deploy.sh; cloud/** merges briefly 503 the CP; .ex waits for the Elixir Test gate; the 49-check offline deploy harness stays green and GAINS rollback cases; worktrees from origin/main after git fetch; builders claim first; PR body carries 'Task: <id>'; file all tasks under self-update-epic.

Wave ledger

Slice tasks: none yet — Decide files them. This section names every task id this wave drives once they exist.

Survey digest (Digest phase, 2026-07-11)

Established beyond doubt (file:line evidence in the survey reports). (1) SLOT-VERSION AMNESIA is real: .instance-deploy-last holds one global sha (instance-deploy.sh:59,290); .slots/*.env carry only PORT_OVERRIDE+MIX_BUILD_ROOT (:189-190); nothing records what the idle slot's build corresponds to, and the NEXT deploy rm -rf's exactly that build (:199). Rollback needs a per-slot version stamp written at deploy time and must refuse when it is missing. (2) WORSE THAN THE CHARTER ASSUMED — both slots run `mix phx.server` against ONE SHARED git checkout (barkpark-slot@.service:15-16 -> api/start.sh:36-38); MIX_BUILD_ROOT isolates only the _build cache, and the checkout is never reset back on a successful deploy. Restarting the idle slot after HEAD moved forward likely triggers Mix to recompile NEW source into the OLD slot's build root — the 'instant manual rollback' comment (:264-265) is asserted, never tested. This is the single biggest design threat and is INFERRED, not yet proven; the verify fleet proves or refutes it. (3) Shared-static hazard confirmed in the script's own words (:216-217): priv/static + the per-deploy-rebuilt wasm blob are shared into both slots — a flip serves old beam with newest assets. (4) Schema stays forward: one ecto.migrate on the NEW build (:204-205); expand/contract is a 3-place comment convention (deploy/README.md:29-30, instance-deploy.sh:16-17, cp-deploy.sh:15), unenforced, scoped to the swap window; the health gate is a shallow /api/schemas 200 (:234) — rollback copy must say app-level-only and what the gate does NOT prove. (5) The post-flip public curl (:260) is LOG-ONLY — copying it as rollback's gate would be a fake gate; the real gate is the pre-flip localhost loop (:232-243).

Relay + pin + truth loop, fully mapped. Console button -> CP POST /v1/barkparks/:id/self-update (require_primary_team_admin, team-scoped 404, router.ex:1787) -> Registry.trigger_self_update (pin gate, Vault-decrypted per-instance admin token, synchronous :httpc 15s) -> instance POST /v1/admin/self-update (require_admin) -> Runner async OS Port -> scripts/self-update.sh -> exec deploy/instance-deploy.sh on .slots boxes. Rollback rides this exact chain as a sibling verb and MUST keep the async-Port shape (the CP relay times out at 15s). pinned_release is an unvalidated <=255-char string with exactly two readers: trigger refusal (registry.ex:2678) and rollout-worker candidate exclusion (is_nil, registry.ex:2791) — so a PINNED rollback is already immune to re-advancement with zero new logic, and an UNPINNED rollback is actively undone within one 5-min tick. The pin value must come from what the instance REPORTS it rolled back to, never operator free-text, and the existing pin gate must not block rollback (rollback re-pins by design). Version truth: BuildInfo is compile-time — the old slot reports the old release correctly once booted; the CP sees it at the hourly :17 cron unless the rollback route mirrors the trigger's schedule_in:60 UpdateStatusWorker enqueue + push_event('fleet'). A SECOND lying surface exists: barkpark-agent's git_commit = shared checkout HEAD (60s beat, report.go) — it lies after a bare flip unless the rollback resets checkout HEAD or the probe becomes slot-aware.

Operator gate resolved by evidence, not invention. Three principal models exist; the require_worker fleet routes (kill switch, channel) are operator-UNREACHABLE in production — the console probe noBounce-hides its own 401 (app.js:3499-3506) and bp cloud rollout sends an ordinary session token that can never equal WORKER_TOKEN (client.go:1647-1661); the Go tests are vacuous-green (fakeCP never checks Authorization). Rollback targets one team-owned instance, so it uses require_primary_team_admin — the ONE gate genuinely reachable from both console and bp CLI today. No third principal model. The kill-switch unreachability is a pre-existing gap to file, not to silently repeat.

Surfaces + harness. Offline harness deploy/instance-deploy_test.sh has 68 checks TODAY (the wish's '49' is stale — correct all acceptance criteria), PATH-shim fakes with caddy the one real binary, zero rollback or migration cases; the forward path's Caddyfile backup/restore idiom (:246-259) is directly reusable for fail-closed cases, and the single global HEALTH_CODE fake suffices for the three deny cases. CLI: NO `bp cloud update` trigger verb exists (the console chip promising it at app.js:3847 is a tested promise with no backing code) — bp cloud rollback is brand-new surface: cloud_rollback_cmd.go, dispatched from runCloud in hetzner_cmd.go (NOT cloud_cmd.go, a naming decoy), modeled on cloud_verify_cmd.go (typed refusals, exit-follows-verdict, raw-envelope -o json). Console: the isu-w5 update panel (app.js ~3130-3465) is the exact clone template — distinct rollback-named modal functions, __bpTestHook exports, mandatory escaping tests for any server string rendered.

Charter + prior art reconciled. The live charter slot is .claude/workflows/bp-self-update-w5-charter.md (its own header says so; bp-cloud-epic-charter.md now holds the parity-page epic). OC10's 2026-07-09 spike rejected PIN-DOWNGRADE rollback (git ff-only makes downgrade impossible) — that verdict is about a SIBLING dead end and does NOT disprove the port-flip design; Decide should state this explicitly so nobody conflates them. No W6 task is filed yet; the design is genuinely greenfield. Smoke reality: golive-test.barkpark.cloud exists nowhere (repo or DNS); the staging BOX is human-gated (separate Hetzner DNS token); a live smoke needs no real DNS anyway (instance-deploy.sh:259 curl --resolve trick) — park it as a recipe against a disposable warm-image box (staging charter D2 pattern). Guerrilla is production AND this workflow's own task ledger — never the first flip.

(a) slot-machinery-truth calls origin/fix/self-update-slot-box (d889aa08) UNMERGED and says it 'teaches' self-update.sh the .slots delegation — but update-relay-seam and scripts-triple both read that delegation ON MAIN (self-update.sh:61-66). (b) deny-path-semantics could not find the console consumer of error.pinned_release — resolved: it greped only .tsx/.ts/.jsx/.heex and the console is vanilla cloud/priv/static/app.js (openUpdateConflictModal); no verify needed. (c) 49 vs 68 harness checks — resolved by running: 68.

Coverage map — checked and NOT found (absences are decisions-in-waiting). NOT found anywhere: any rollback verb/route/CLI/script (greenfield confirmed repo-wide); a per-slot version stamp; a migration-safety linter or CI gate for expand/contract; a `bp cloud update` trigger verb; a platform-admin session principal (PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS is digest-recipient-only, 'this var alone can't open a relay'); golive-test.barkpark.cloud; any staging-channel registry row (inferred — could not authenticate to the CP to live-confirm); pinned_release format/existence validation; harness coverage of migrate or of restarting a retired slot.
